label: <DEL> step, when the sequence contains several of n/1/j/v/c/t
explanation: Almost only fires at the delimiter step: 99.9% of activation mass is at <DEL>, and it is active on about 12.6% of <DEL> steps. It almost never fires in the original phase, and in the copy phase only rarely at recall_idx 1, mostly when the first token is h. Which <DEL> steps fire depends on what came before: firing is more likely in longer sequences (rate goes up steadily with L, from 0.6% to 1.3% of steps, and L 8-9 carries 62% of mass), when the prefix contains several of n, 1, j, v, c, t, and when the first token is b, i, g or p (b has the most mass). The predicate (<DEL> and at least 2 of those tokens seen) gets about 84% of mass but precision is only about 0.26. This looks like a distributed readout of the prefix contents rather than a clean rule. Adding a first-token clause raises dev F1 only to about 0.45.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: b, i, p, g, u, 2; least: e, y, -, c) and the third original token (most: n, 1, c, v, k, j; least: g, i, m, b); timing cues that raise it most: phase=1, recall_idx=0, recall_idx=1.
